title: The EU has new rules on immigrants

paragraphs: The European leaders voted to approve a new law to increase sending illegal immigrants away. The vote passed with 418 politicians in favor and 218 against.

After the vote, right-wing politicians celebrated and shouted ‚send them back‘ inside the government building. This made left-wing politicians very angry, and they shouted back ,shame on you.‘ The event showed that European leaders don’t agree on immigration. Some groups and experts strongly criticize the new rules. They say the plan is cruel because it allows the government to lock up people for two years or send them to faraway centers.
Right-wing leaders are happy and say they are showing their power. Other politicians say this reaction is bad and makes people hate each other more.

words.d: to accept a plan, law, or idea officially
to support or agree with an idea or law in a vote

paragraphs: Leaders in Europe vote on a new law. They want to send illegal immigrants out of their countries.
Many people in the government vote for the law. They are very happy. They stand up and shout. Other people are angry. This shows that the leaders have very different ideas.

Many groups say that the new law is bad and unkind. It allows the government to put people in prison for two years. Some leaders say that this day is a dark time in the history of Europe. They think that the new rules will hurt families and children.

words.d: a person who comes to live in another country

paragraphs: The European Parliament has approved new measures aimed at increasing the deportation of undocumented people. This sparked a heated confrontation among lawmakers.

An alliance of centre-right and far-right politicians voted 418 to 218 in favor of the overhaul. Following the vote, right-wing lawmakers celebrated by jumping to their feet, pumping their fists, and chanting ‚send them back‘. In response, leftwing and centre-left politicians shouted back ‚shame on you‘, which showed deep political divisions.

Human rights groups and UN experts have strongly criticized the plan and called it cruel and discriminatory. The new rules allow for people to be detained for up to two years or sent to offshore centres, which critics call human rights black holes. While far-right leaders welcomed the vote as a successful show of political force, opponents warned of hatred and damage to democratic institutions. They marked it a dark moment in European history.

words.d: a group of people, political parties, or countries that agree to work together to achieve something
a complete change to a system or a law to fix it or make it work in a brand new way
a deep and serious disagreement between two groups of people that separates them
unfair because it treats a specific group of people worse than others based on who they are
